title: Chapter 142: All Roads Lead to the Same Place
html:
The game sounded harmless at first, but its implications were deeply unsettling.

“The monster climbed onto your brother’s shoulders and grew even taller?” Chen Ge struggled to imagine a 2.6-meter figure balanced on a child.

“That’s what Shenglong wrote. We asked him to draw it too.” Wang Hailong took out his phone. “He made this from memory during his last doctor’s visit.”

The drawing was bizarre. A short, chubby child occupied the bottom tenth of the page; the creature on his shoulders filled everything else.

“What is that?” The creature had a woman’s unruly hair but a man’s body, thin as two bamboo poles beneath a white sheet.

“Don’t you recognize it? I saw something similar in your Haunted House—a girl standing on people’s shoulders. It reminded me of Shenglong’s story.” Wang Hailong reclaimed the phone and looked toward the attraction, fear returning to his eyes. “You must have experienced something like this to create the scene. And when the girl stood on me, the weight felt real. If I knew any less, I’d swear I met a ghost.”

“We use advanced 4D technology and special techniques to engage all five senses. That’s why you felt weight on your shoulders,” Chen Ge lied without shame. “The resemblance is coincidence.”

“Fine.” But Wang Hailong did not give up. “Then, can you tell me what it is that inspired you to create such a scene?”

Wang Hailong was stubborn.

After some thought, Chen Ge said, “Ghosts are products of the imagination. I understand your concern, but I’m not a doctor. You should consult a psychologist. I can recommend one.”

With the park potentially closing in two months, Chen Ge could not waste time on irrelevant matters. More importantly, he had no psychological training. A professional would serve Shenglong better.

“Our father has taken him to psychologists since childhood. A psychiatric hospital stood near our old home, and Shenglong spent some time there, but the treatment accomplished little.” Wang Hailong hesitated.

“Let me explain.” Wang Wenlong steadied his brother. “For some reason, Shenglong has a severe aversion to doctors. When someone in medical clothing approaches, he screams, struggles, and sometimes becomes violent. We have to warn every new physician in advance.”

“An aversion to doctors?” This was the second anomaly. “Could the thing on his shoulders fear doctors and hurt him whenever one approaches?”

“We don’t know. Before his admission, doctors didn’t frighten him. The fear began after he left that hospital,” Wang Wenlong said, revealing a secret the family had kept for years.

“Such a sudden change must have a cause. Could something during treatment have traumatized him?”

“Impossible. Shenglong was so young that family remained with him constantly. The doctors treated him well.”

“Then perhaps the environment caused it. Return to the old hospital; you may find clues there.” Having offered his advice, Chen Ge turned toward lunch.

“The hospital closed years ago. The third building, where Shenglong stayed, is completely sealed. We couldn’t enter even if we tried.” Wang Hailong sighed. “I’m sorry for unloading this on you. Too much today reminded us of him.”

“The third building?” The black phone’s mission had made Chen Ge acutely sensitive to the word. “Which hospital?”

“The one beside our old home, in the neighboring district. We were poor and couldn’t afford anywhere else. Once our finances improved, we transferred him.”

“I mean its name.” The intensity in Chen Ge’s eyes unsettled Wang Hailong.

“Jiujiang Third Psychological Convalescence Center—usually called the Third Center. I think it has been abandoned for five or six years.” Neither brother understood Chen Ge’s sudden intensity.

“Is there a place called the Third Sick Hall at this center?” Chen Ge was lining up the dots in his mind.

“That’s what you mean. Some people called the third building the Third Sick Hall. Different names, same place.”

“I understand.” Chen Ge took in a deep breath. “I know the best doctor in Jiujiang. If possible, can you bring me to meet your little brother tonight?”

Before they could refuse, Chen Ge began praising Doctor Gao’s credentials.

“No problem, but prepare yourself. My brother… doesn’t look normal.” Wang Hailong forced a smile. “If the doctor comes, ask him to dress casually.”

He produced a black business card bearing the words “Long Hu Fang.”

“You are…?” The unusual card and the tattoos covering both brothers finally clicked in Chen Ge’s mind.

Are they gang members?He had never dealt with organized criminals before.

Seeing Chen Ge’s shock, Wang Hailong lowered his voice. “It’s exactly what you think. My family owns Long Hu Fang Sichuan Hot Pot. The phone number is on the back.”

Chen Ge flashed a bright smile as he accepted the card. “Do you have a more specific address?”

“Come to Hai Ming Apartments in the old district tonight. Shenglong lives there with our father.”
